# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

# Complete large finite XPath repetition delivery

## Issue and governing contract

Deliver the full body and both comments of #467 on the isolated current-main
successor. The dated XPath 2.0 and 3.1 matchers must answer every reported
large finite-count shape at production limits through Rust, CLI, Python, C,
and the optimized shipped WASM package. Counts must not multiply work per
input byte. Matching, leftmost priority, captures, replacement, dated syntax
and flags, and operational failure semantics remain the existing laws.

Root AGENTS.md, .baseline, and .goals apply: one original engine and storage
owner, no new dependency or semantic feature, actual admission before native
growth, hard typed failures, no scope cuts or deficiencies, deterministic
output, normal signed hooks, protected main and all donor/sibling work. The
current user AGENTS has no fixed gate-count or reviewer-count rule. Required
checks repeat only for relevant changes or failures. No governing ADR was
found or cited by the full intake. The change-path allocations and prepared
products design documents govern native ownership and reusable compilation.

## Prior art and coverage

The complete stagectl brief captured issue #467, its two comments, linked
closed #406, and four related forge items. Its bounded last-200-commit trailer
census reports none=23, performance=2, semantic-identity-loss=1; those are
repository trailer counts, not a regex defect rate.

The preserved branch paudley/406-large-count-followup has one explicitly
unfinished commit efd2829a6 on 36a13ac79. It changes the original compiler,
backtracking/Pike/set machine homes plus host fixtures and benches. Reuse
its complete algorithmic delta, evaluating both it and current main at each
changed owner. It predates the landed native compile/match storage controls;
its raw reservations and old cell accounting are not acceptable unchanged.
The donor branch remains untouched. Existing main contains the dated laws,
independent finite-language fixtures, forced backtracking/thread/set paths,
native owned pattern and execution carriers, and actual host entry points.

## Design

1. Keep the flat compiled Node arena and existing matcher dispatch. Extend
   its original Links facts with single-character choices/capture chains,
   qualifying large nonnullable repeats, and their original owned arrays.
   Following-character/end facts remain conservative source-order facts.
2. An execution may ignore a finite maximum strictly beyond the input-derived
   bound on completed iterations. The existing progress law limits empty
   iterations to those below the minimum and one stopping empty iteration.
   Compatibility nullable bodies retain their finite maximum because their
   ordered empty-iteration capture histories can distinguish it.
   Use checked/widened arithmetic and preserve exact bounds when they can
   decide a choice. Unicode inputs count characters through byte positions;
   a byte bound is conservative, never a lower bound on available characters.
3. Greedy bodies consuming exactly one character, with no branching capture
   distinction, scan once and keep one descending-stop continuation. Preserve
   source priority, final-iteration capture chains, follow anchors/multiline
   behavior, UTF-8 boundaries, reluctant/general alternatives, and repeated
   search reuse. Credit only genuinely new linear scan work to the existing
   bounded attempt; do not change production resource ceilings.
4. Qualifying large nonnullable counted set states use the donor's relative
   count offsets only when transitions are certified insensitive to the
   original bounds. Restore exact absolute counts at sensitive boundaries,
   reverse checkpoints, splits, and acceptance. Keep every original state,
   offset, cache, checkpoint and spill array under Budget's native admission
   before growth; destruction/refunds must preserve first failure and retained
   compiled/execution output lifetimes.
5. The existing backtracking reference must bypass the newly optimized run,
   input-bound collapse and relative-cache routes when used as the independent
   randomized oracle. Use the original general repetition law at its existing
   home, not a copied second evaluator. The forced thread path and explicit
   finite languages add independent controls. Required comparison cases must
   complete; silently skipping operationally refused oracle cases is not proof.
6. Host tests call the actual dated REGEX/REPLACE surfaces. The optimized WASM
   acceptance exercises the packaged module after wasm-opt and post-linking,
   not merely a native Rust test of exports. New genuine language-surface test
   files carry the required Why not Rust explanation; do not grow ratcheted
   existing Python/JS files or move old tests to evade the ratchet.
7. Replace false universal prose with measured, named fixture evidence from
   settled code. Preserve resource codes/ceilings and actual nested-nullable
   and backreference refusals. State that remaining count combinations can
   cost work or storage; no new universal performance/admission promise.

No new public tuning control, second numeric/regex engine, runtime dependency,
arbitrary semantic count ceiling, or separate foundation PR is warranted.
Routing/cache thresholds change cost only and do not limit accepted syntax.

## Completeness contract

All rows belong to Task 1 and must be proven before Task 2 publication.

| Requirement | Actual input and entry | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seven reported positive shapes | 4 MiB inputs; `^[\\s\\S]{0,10000000}$`, `^[^\\n]{0,10000000}$`, `^[^<>]{1,5000000}$`, `^[\\p{L} ]{1,5000000}$`, `^(\\w+\\s?){1,5000000}$`, `^(a\|b){4194304}$`, `(a\|b){4000000}`; core is_match/find, both dated laws | Correct boolean, leftmost whole span and last-iteration captures at unchanged Limits::new(), no resource refusal |
| Replacement | 2 MiB word-group input and exact-count alternation, core replace_all and actual SPARQL REPLACE | Exact final iteration `$1`, unaffected suffix and output-byte refusal law |
| Cost independent of count | Same actual inputs with multiple finite maxima beyond reachable bound, exact counts varied alongside input size; original Budget MatchSteps | Equal steps for nonbinding maxima; a count-independent integer per-byte bound for each named eligible fixture; original low-cost neighbours remain controls |
| Rejection neighbours | Wrong class `<`/`!`, exact count ±1, shorter input, interrupted unanchored run, input beyond binding maximum, multibyte/case/newline flags | Correct false/no match or exact spans, no changed greediness or captures |
| Independent differential | Seeded generated counts below/at/above input and routing boundary, nested/nonnullable/nullable/reluctant/capture/backreference shapes, both laws and flags; original general backtracking, forced thread and production VM | Required completed comparisons, exact spans/captures/search progression/replacement; syntax differences asserted explicitly |
| Relative-state boundary | Counts around normalization margin/routing threshold, forward/reverse scans, repeated searches and deliberately tight checkpoints/cache splits | Same oracle outcome and captures, no stale offset transition |
| Native storage | Owned compiled/match/replace doors with refusing Admission and counting allocator, deep character-choice worklist and new offset/cache arrays | Before-birth typed refusal, no partial publication, first original failure, actual live/peak layout covered and clone/drop release preserved |
| CLI | Actual CLI dated profile REGEX and REPLACE over generated 4 MiB/2 MiB Turtle input, both laws | Exact output booleans and replacement, malformed/operational controls unchanged |
| Python | Installed native Dataset query dated profile via genuine new Python binding tests, same required shapes/sizes and both laws | Exact actual query output and replacement; module built from this source |
| C | Actual purrdf_query_json_xpath_regex and owned C output/status/free API, same required shapes/sizes and both laws | Exact output and statuses, no host-specific behavior |
| Optimized WASM | Genuine JS package test through shipped Dataset/query dated profile, same required shapes/sizes and both laws, optimized wasm-opt/post-link output | Exact output/replacement and typed host refusal; actual package/Node execution |
| Validator consumers | Actual SHACL and ShEx dated pattern facets plus existing native profiles | Large counted positive/negative facets preserve report semantics and operational failures |
| Benches | Original xsd_regex testkit bench target, named 1–4 MiB/count ladders for all seven shapes, decision/find/replacement and neighbours | Durable measured timing/work receipts; benches assert intended results before measuring |
| Truthful descriptions | Limits::new documentation, book diagnostic discussion/table, nested nullable `((a?){3000}){3000}b` vs `((a?){5000}){5000}b` on `aaab` and original examples | Prose/diagnostic meaning matches measured settled work and current refusal classes; no unsupported universal step assertion |
| Whole qualification | Strict affected all-target lints, native family, installed Python, optimized package, metadata/book/i18n and unchanged make check | Terminal PASS receipts bound to settled source; no skipped required host/corpus/gate |

## Task 1: Complete counted repetition behavior and all production acceptance

Implement the coherent donor adaptation in the original compile/match/pike/sets
homes with current native storage. Add full differential, size/cost, allocation,
capture/replacement and validator controls; real CLI/Python/C/optimized-WASM
fixtures and bench lanes. Settle code and fixtures before the first consolidated
affected compilation. Collect the complete family of concrete compiler/runtime
findings, fix them at original owners, and repeat only invalidated checks.

Use a task-private managed target/build/tmp directory and four compiler/test
jobs, MemoryMax=16G, MemorySwapMax=0, after root confirms lane availability.
Preserve sibling processes. Run strict all-target affected compilation followed
by full relevant native suites. Run actual installed Python and optimized WASM
package, not host-shaped native substitutes. Run report-only benches to record
the actual updated work/timing classes before correcting prose. Complete
metadata and affected book/i18n checks through their existing tools.

Root independently reviews the completed whole contract, original native owners
and actual consumer wiring, recording tasks/T1-review.md. Required gaps block
completion. Run the unchanged mandatory make check on settled source; normal
hooks also remain mandatory. Record failures and terminal corrections honestly
in validation.md. Commit the full coherent unit normally with explicit paths,
push normally, and post actual issue evidence. No partial cache/performance PR.

## Task 2: Qualified PR and integration handoff

After every acceptance row and the independent completion judgment is PASS,
prepare the full PR body (Closes #467), uncertainty/reader-not-known notes,
plan/validation/task records, and explicit archive inventory. Create and resolve
the actual PR through stagectl, post the plan and evidence through the authorized
workflow, and return URL/head/remaining hosted status to root. Root owns current
review-debt, final candidate assessment and sequential ghprsq integration.
Preserve source/donor until the successor is accepted and durably archived.

## Current status

Whole local implementation acceptance and mandatory recipe coverage: PASS.
Publication, hosted CI and final integration: NOT MET. Consolidated
affected strict compilation passed on corrected source. The first native
family's actual nullable compatibility capture regression is preserved as a
failed receipt. Its complete correction has passed all 325 tests of the second
full native family, including original-general empty/finite/capture/replacement
controls and the independent compatibility oracle. Fresh installed Python has
passed all 245 cases. All 163 benchmark lanes passed and their raw estimates
are retained. The optimized package's complete Node suite passed all 445 cases
and packed tarball smoke passed; its required dataset/exchange bigint identity
suffix passed, completing the unchanged target with exit 0. Documentation,
metadata, English and Chinese books, glossary/poison controls and all six actual
translated rendering gates passed. The unchanged mandatory make check found
an identical sorted-pair lookup at the regex and IDNA homes. A single lookup
at the existing lexical association home replaces both private bodies without
changing comparison, allocation, counters or lookup outcomes. The complete
affected strict/lexical/IDNA/regex/storage/helper correction family terminated
PASS. The unchanged full-check-2 completed all workspace runtime and doctest
targets, failing only ten missing private-build cache-marker tests in four
targets. After correcting that directory setup without source changes,
full-check-2-continuation.result=0 qualifies all four unchanged targets (112
tests) and the exact unreached consumer/doctest, ring-fence and release-WASM
recipe. Both original failed whole-gate receipts remain preserved.
Independent complete planning judgment: PASS in reviews/plan-review.md. The
whole coherent implementation and meaningful native/host/bench fixtures are
written and locally qualified; the existing independent complete source/contract
judgment is PASS against final terminal evidence. Normal signed hooks and push
passed for 73b0cdae173d98cba92dc4a69031bdb419c23677. The actual clean fetched
candidate and its eight disjoint renderer base paths preserve acceptance
applicability. PR creation, hosted/debt qualification and protected integration
remain pending.

The part I am least confident about is predicting cost for arbitrary nested
count combinations outside the named eligible forms. Relative-state reuse is
the most intricate implementation path; its source law, original-general count
boundaries, absolute thread reference, tight reverse checkpoints, cache splits,
UTF-8/flag/capture cases and real native ownership controls are all required
acceptance. Measured timings are specific to the qualified host and artifact.

The practical distinction a reader should know is that eliminating count-
multiplied work for these forms does not eliminate every operational refusal.
On the actual `aaab` control, nested nullable count 3000 answers while 5000 still
refuses; source bytes, compilation, matching storage/work and output have
independent limits. Those refusals retain their typed cause and publish no
partial answer. The unselected compatibility law also retains its own nullable
capture priority rather than inheriting the dated count collapse.

The two aggregate review items have been checked against the settled source and
completed evidence.

The shared sorted lookup remains in this change because the mandatory one-home
gate found the same body at the new regex set-state producer and the existing
IDNA producer. Both now call the original lexical association home, and both
private copies were removed. Comparisons, absence behavior and the IDNA table are
unchanged; the lookup allocates nothing. The affected strict/lexical/IDNA/regex/
storage family and unchanged helper/hash gates passed. Reverting that move would
restore the prohibited duplicate implementation, so the scope warning is declined.

The randomized differential was executed. The original
`large_and_exact_counts_agree_across_machines_flags_and_laws` case uses fixed
SplitMix64 seed `0x0047_2600_BE4C_0009` to generate inputs and count choices across
pattern templates, five flag selections and both dated laws. It compares actual
production spans/captures and successive searches against the original general
backtracking body and independent thread body; a refused oracle fails the case.
That case, the longer seeded-input comparison and original-general routing/
offset boundary comparison all passed in the complete325-case native family.
The original general body bypasses the new run/count/relative-state shortcuts.
These completed controls answer the inconclusive-evidence item without repeating
an unchanged suite.

Current-head hosted qualification is still pending. No local result or this
feedback disposition is being presented as merged completion.
